title: Bulldog of Aquin
html_source:
Saint Thomas Aquinas (1225—1274)
Aquinas rejects the notions from Arianism and Sabellianism, and proposes that there are three persons in God, with distinctive roles but of the same divine substance. Aquinas is very cautious here in his selection of his words, as he states that to avoid the error of Arius and Sabellius, “we must shun the use of terms diversity and difference in God” and that “we must shun the term “singularity.” Thus, the core idea of Aquinas regarding Trinity is the “unity of essence” and “communicability of the divine essence.”
Paul Kang, The Doctrine of the Holy Trinity
